# Intake brief — When player shoots enemy bullet it should explode

## Problem statement

When a player bullet intercepts an enemy bullet, both projectiles are destroyed **silently** — there is no sound effect (SFX) and no visual effect (VFX) at the point of impact. The player gets no feedback that an incoming shot was successfully shot down, so the interception reads as a missed/ignored collision rather than a skill-rewarding action.

## Users

- **Player** — wants clear, satisfying feedback when they shoot down an incoming enemy bullet.
  - *As a player, when my bullet destroys an enemy bullet I hear and see a small impact, so I know my shot connected and the threat is gone.*
- **Developer / designer** — wants one shared implementation used by both the shipped game and the gym scenes.
  - *As a developer, I want the bullet-impact feedback implemented in shared code so the game (`PlayScene`) and the gyms (`GymFormationScene`) cannot drift apart.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Dedicated bullet-destruction SFX.** When a player bullet overlaps an enemy bullet, a **new dedicated** `playBulletDestructionSound()` plays exactly once at the impact point. The shared enemy-destruction `playDestructionSound()` is **not** invoked for this event. Verified by a unit test spying on the audio module.
- [ ] **AC2 — Small impact VFX.** A small, short-lived flash/glow VFX appears at the impact point and is cleaned up when it finishes. The full `spawnExplosionParticles()` particle burst is **not** used for bullet destruction. Verified by a unit test asserting the impact effect is created and torn down.
- [ ] **AC3 — Shared code path (no game/gym divergence).** The bullet-vs-bullet impact feedback is implemented in a single shared helper/module and invoked by **both** `PlayScene._handleCollisions()` (case 2) and `GymFormationScene._handleCollisions()` (case 2) — the behaviour is identical in the shipped game and the gym. Verified by both call sites referencing the shared helper and by a test in each scene suite.
- [ ] **AC4 — No double feedback on player hit.** When an enemy bullet instead reaches the player, only the existing `_hitPlayer()` feedback fires; the enemy bullet is not also given the bullet-destruction SFX/VFX. Verified by a regression test.
- [ ] **AC5 — Test coverage (validation).** New/updated unit tests assert: the dedicated SFX fires once per interception (and not the generic cue); the impact VFX is created and cleaned up; both scenes route through the shared helper; and no double-play on player hit. Identical inputs remain deterministic.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — in particular `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.2 (VFX) and §7.3 (SFX event catalogue) must record the new bullet-destruction cue.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** Run the complete suite (`/skill:test`) and confirm zero failures.

## Constraints

- **Dedicated cue.** The new SFX must be a *new* function in `src/audio/effects.ts` (per producer decision), synthesised with the existing `blip()` helper. Short, higher-pitched and low-volume so it reads as a light "tick" and does not mask the heavier destruction cue. Must be a safe no-op without an `AudioContext` (headless tests / autoplay-blocked browsers).
- **Small VFX only.** Bullets are ~3 px radius; the effect must be a brief flash/glow, **not** the full particle-burst system (`spawnExplosionParticles()` is explicitly out per producer answer Q2).
- **No feedback on player hit.** Do **not** add a separate explosion when the enemy bullet reaches the player — `_hitPlayer()`'s SFX + VFX already covers that collision (producer answer Q3).
- **Shared implementation.** Implement through a shared helper/module so `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` exercise the same code (producer follow-up #2: "They should share all code"). Do not add two divergent copies.
- **Narrow refactor.** Extract only what is needed for the bullet-vs-bullet impact feedback. Do not consolidate the wider duplicated collision logic here — that is tracked separately in AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO.
- Preserve all existing collision semantics, hit radii (`PLAYER_BULLET_RADIUS`, enemy-bullet radius 5) and consumption behaviour (both bullets are destroyed).

## Existing state

- `PlayScene._handleCollisions()` case 2 (player bullets vs enemy bullets) destroys both bullets with no SFX/VFX (~`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` line 1018).
- `GymFormationScene._handleCollisions()` case 2 has the identical silent behaviour (~`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` line 1463).
- `src/audio/effects.ts` exposes `playDestructionSound()` (0.28 s sawtooth sweep, volume 0.3) and the reusable `blip()` synthesis helper. There is **no** bullet-destruction sound.
- `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` exposes `spawnExplosionParticles()` for full particle bursts (used for entity/player destruction).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.3 lists "Player bullet hits enemy — Very short tick, Low volume" but has no bullet-vs-bullet entry; §7.2 covers particle explosions.
- There is no shared combat/collision module: the only two `_handleCollisions` implementations live in the two scenes above.

## Desired change

- Add a dedicated `playBulletDestructionSound()` to `src/audio/effects.ts` (short, higher-pitched, low-volume blip).
- Add a small impact-VFX helper (e.g. a brief flash/glow graphic that fades and destroys itself) — a new shared module such as `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts`.
- Extract a shared bullet-vs-bullet impact helper (e.g. `resolveBulletVsBulletImpact(scene, x, y)`) that plays the cue and spawns the VFX, and call it from case 2 of **both** `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` when a player bullet consumes an enemy bullet.
- Add/update unit tests for the SFX, the VFX, and both call sites; update the GDD §7.2/§7.3 documentation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Add `playBulletDestructionSound()`; export any tuning constants.
- `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts` (new) — Shared small flash/glow impact VFX helper.
- `src/scenes/combat/` or equivalent (new, if preferred) — Shared bullet-vs-bullet impact resolution helper used by both scenes.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Call the shared helper in `_handleCollisions()` case 2.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Call the shared helper in `_handleCollisions()` case 2.
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` — Assert the new cue's synthesis/no-op behaviour.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — Assert dedicated SFX fired once, VFX spawned, no generic cue, no double-play on player hit.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — Assert the same shared behaviour in the gym.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Update §7.2 (VFX) and §7.3 (SFX event catalogue).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (confirmed):** "dedicated" means a new exported sound function, not reuse of `playDestructionSound()`.
- **Assumption:** "simpler VFX" means a brief flash/glow — no particle burst — and it need not be extensible to entities.
- **Risk — audio cacophony:** dense bullet patterns can produce many interceptions; the cue must be short and low-volume to avoid stacking (see GDD §6.7 SFX rate-limiting).
- **Risk — shared-helper placement:** both scenes are large; extracting into a clearly named shared module avoids a new divergent copy. Keep the change surgical.
- **Risk — scope creep:** the duplicated `_handleCollisions` logic in the two scenes is a wider problem; it is deliberately excluded and tracked in **AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO** so this item stays focused.
- **Risk — test coupling:** scene suites boot Phaser; assert via the shared helper and audio-module spies rather than pixel-level VFX inspection.

## Related work

Manual (genuinely relevant):

- **AH-0MU0AVBWH002ZWRH** — Add randomness to explosion (in-progress, high): touches the same `playDestructionSound()`/explosion SFX area; the new bullet cue should not conflict with its randomisation scope.
- **AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M** — Restore gym-game parity (completed, epic): the RCA that established gym/game parity as a recurring concern; this item follows the same "prefer shared code" constraint.
- **AH-0MTECNG4K0071TIB** / **AH-0MTECNG8W00403EH** — Core scene collision tests/implementation (completed): cover player-bullet-destroys-enemy-bullet behaviour without feedback.
- **AH-0MU4KJZUE001X6LD** — Extract shared bullet creation utility function (completed): precedent for shared bullet utilities.
- **AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO** — Consolidate duplicated PlayScene/GymFormationScene collision logic (open, discovered-from this item): the wider duplication this item deliberately does not tackle.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MT7QQGBU008V4R0** – Write the Game Design Document (completed)
- **AH-0MU7JTG9R002ZWA6** – Wave time limit: surviving enemies detonate at 10x scale and cost a life (completed)
- **AH-0MTECNI1Y001O2OV** – Test: Core scene — enemy live aim tracking (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `standups/2026_09_22.md` — matched: bullet, enemy, explode, explosions, player (+5 more)
- `README.md` — matched: bullet, enemy, explode, player, sfx (+3 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: bullet, enemy, explode, player, sfx (+3 more)

## Appendix — Clarifying questions & answers

Round 1 (asked 2026-09-16, answered 2026-09-17):

- **Q1 — SFX: reuse `playDestructionSound()` or a distinct cue?**
  Answer: **same** — reuse the existing `playDestructionSound()` (shared with enemy entities). *Superseded (see follow-up Q1).*
- **Q2 — VFX: existing `spawnExplosionParticles()` burst or a simpler effect?**
  Answer (producer): **simpler** — not the full particle burst; a brief flash or glow is preferred, given bullets are ~3 px radius. Research: `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` `spawnExplosionParticles()` is a size-scaled full burst (base count 30, clamped 8–80) — visually too heavy for a 3 px bullet.
- **Q3 — Scope: should the enemy bullet also explode when it hits the player?**
  Answer (producer): **no** — the existing `_hitPlayer()` SFX + VFX for the player is sufficient at the collision point.
- **Q4 — Consistency: dedicated sound or the generic one?**
  Answer: **dedicated** — bullet destruction should have its own dedicated sound cue, not reuse `playDestructionSound()`. *(Conflicted with Q1; see follow-up Q1.)*

Follow-up round (asked 2026-09-22, answered 2026-09-22) — resolves the Q1/Q4 contradiction:

- **Follow-up Q1 — Which SFX answer wins, Q1 ("same") or Q4 ("dedicated")?**
  Answer (producer): **Dedicated.** Create a bullet-specific cue — do not reuse `playDestructionSound()`. Source: interactive reply.
- **Follow-up Q2 — Scope: shipped game only, or should the gym core be mirrored?**
  Answer (producer): "There shouldn't be different core code in the shipped game and the gym scenes. They should share all code." Source: interactive reply. Research: `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` each define their own `_handleCollisions` (no shared combat module), so the impact feedback must be delivered through a shared helper used by both; wider consolidation of the duplicated collision logic is a separate follow-up (AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO, discovered-from this item).

Open questions: none — all clarifications answered.

# Leaderboard: Game-Over Score Entry and localStorage Display

## Problem Statement

The game currently has no scoring system, no game-over screen, and no leaderboard. When the player runs out of lives, the game respawns infinitely with no termination. The player has no way to record or view their high scores.

## Users

- **Player**: Completes the game (or dies) and wants to record their score by entering 3-character initials. They want to see their scores ranked against previous attempts on the game-over screen and from the main menu.

### User Stories

- As a player, when I run out of lives, I want to see my final score and be prompted to enter my initials so I can record my achievement.
- As a player, after entering my initials, I want to see the full leaderboard ranked by score so I can see how I compare to my past scores.
- As a player, from the main menu, I want to view the leaderboard to see my best scores.

## Original Acceptance Criteria (superseded 2026-09-22)

1. **Score tracking**: Each enemy type has a defined `scoreValue`. When an enemy is destroyed, its `scoreValue` is added to the player's total score. The score is displayed in the HUD (top-right corner, neon-styled numeric display).

2. **Game-over condition**: When the player's lives reach 0 (starting at 3, max 5 via P8 Extra Life), the game stops respawning and transitions to the game-over screen. There is no continue mechanic. The game-over screen shows the final score, an option to save (if score qualifies), and a restart button.

3. **Initials entry**: On the game-over screen, the player is prompted to enter exactly 3 uppercase letters (A-Z) as initials. Input is validated (only A-Z accepted, exactly 3 characters). [ASSUMPTION: on-screen clickable keyboard styled to match the neon terminal aesthetic.]

4. **localStorage persistence**: Entries are stored in browser localStorage under the key `ai_hell_leaderboard`. The stored data is a JSON array of entry objects (max 10 entries). When a new score qualifies for the leaderboard (i.e., would rank within the top 10), the player can enter initials to save it. If the score does not qualify, the player is informed and may skip the entry.

5. **Leaderboard display**: The game-over screen displays the full leaderboard showing rank, initials, score, and date for each entry, sorted by score (highest first). The leaderboard is also accessible from the main menu.

## Constraints

- Browser `localStorage` only (no backend, per GDD §5.1 — "single-machine" MVP).
- Maximum 10 leaderboard entries.
- Initials must be exactly 3 characters, uppercase letters only.
- Date format: ISO YYYY-MM-DD (per GDD data model example).
- The leaderboard data structure must support future abstraction for online leaderboards (GDD §5.3 migration note).

## Existing State

- **No score tracking exists**: No `scoreValue` on enemies, no score counter, no score display.
- **No game-over condition**: The `GymFormationScene` has infinite respawn — when all enemies are wiped, the formation respawns regardless of player lives.
- **Lives tracking exists**: `EffectsRegistry` tracks lives (starts at 3, caps at 5), displayed via the HUD. But lives are never decremented on player death.
- **No main menu**: The only entry scene is `GymIndex` (dev-mode gym scene launcher). No `MainMenuScene` exists.
- **No leaderboard code**: No localStorage operations for leaderboard, no initials input, no game-over screen.
- **GDD references**: `src/core/GameState.ts` and `src/scenes/Menu.ts` are predicted but not yet implemented.

## Desired Change

1. **`src/core/Leaderboard.ts`** — Leaderboard persistence module:
   - `getEntries()`: Read and parse entries from localStorage.
   - `addEntry(initials: string, score: number)`: Add a new entry, maintain max 10, sort by score.
   - `getTopN(n: number)`: Return top N entries.
   - `isQualifying(score: number)`: Check if score would make the top 10.
   - Data structure: `{ rank, initials, score, date }` per GDD §5.2.

2. **Score tracking in `GymFormationScene`**:
   - Assign `scoreValue` to each enemy type (Scout: 100, Diver: 150, Tank: 200, Phaser: 300, Swarm: 50 per, Boss: 1000 — [ASSUMPTION values, to be confirmed]).
   - Track player score as a counter in the scene.
   - Add score to total on enemy destroy.
   - Display score in the HUD (top-right).

3. **Game-over screen (`src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts`)**:
   - Displays final score, player initials input, and leaderboard.
   - Neon-styled UI matching the game aesthetic.
   - On-screen 3x3 grid keyboard for initials entry.
   - "Submit" button validates and saves the entry.
   - "Restart" button returns to the main menu (or GymIndex for now).

4. **Main menu (`src/scenes/MainMenuScene.ts`)**:
   - "Play" button to start the game.
   - "Leaderboard" button to view the full leaderboard.
   - "Gym" button to access the gym index.
   - [NOTE: Main menu creation scope — see open questions.]

5. **Lives integration**:
   - Decrement lives on player hit (when invulnerable period ends).
   - When lives reach 0, transition to game-over screen.
   - Stop the respawn loop when game-over is triggered.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope risk — main menu creation**: Creating a full main menu scene is a significant addition. If scope is constrained, the leaderboard may be accessible from the existing GymIndex instead, with the main menu deferred to a separate work item.
- **Scope risk — score tracking from scratch**: No score infrastructure exists. Implementing scoreValue on all enemy types, the score counter, and HUD display adds non-trivial work to GymFormationScene.
- **Assumption — enemy score values**: The GDD defines `scoreValue` on enemies but does not specify numeric values. The values in the draft are estimates and should be tuned.
- **Assumption — keyboard UI**: On-screen clickable keyboard was assumed; a producer decision is needed on input mechanism.
- **Assumption — game-over restart flow**: "Restart" returns to main menu (or GymIndex if no main menu). No "Play Again" shortcut from game-over.
- **Scope guard**: Level progression, boss mechanics, difficulty scaling, online leaderboards, and persistent game state between sessions are out of scope.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/Leaderboard.ts` — New file: leaderboard localStorage persistence
- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts` — New file: game-over screen with initials input and leaderboard display
- `src/scenes/MainMenuScene.ts` — New file: main menu with leaderboard access [scope TBD]
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Modify: add score tracking, game-over condition, lives decrement
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — Modify: add score display (top-right)
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` / `src/entities/*.ts` — Modify: add `scoreValue` to enemy types
- `src/core/Game.ts` — Modify: register new scenes, update boot flow
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — Modify: add MainMenu/GameOver to scene list for shipped build

## Related Work

- **AH-0MTZWZ1MQ004L552**: Create a playable game (parent epic, high priority, in `idea` stage) — includes main menu and playable game scope. This work item is a child of this epic.
- **AH-0MU3VOQKH005YOBH**: Combat gym scenes — uses the same `GymFormationScene` base.
- **AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ**: Gym index scene (completed) — current entry point.
- **AH-0MU6VSKZT006HBTR**: Leaderboard — discovered-from the playable-game epic; the GDD (§5) is the authoritative spec.
- **GDD §5**: Leaderboard design document — authoritative spec.
- **GDD §4.5**: Game-over conditions — 3 lives, no continue, score submission.
- **GDD §6.4**: Technical architecture — predicted `src/core/GameState.ts` and `src/scenes/Menu.ts`.
- **AH-0MU3VOQKH005YOBH**: Combat gym scenes (gym scenes where power-up layer is shared) — uses the same `GymFormationScene` base.
- **AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ**: Gym index scene (completed) — current entry point.
- **GDD §5**: Leaderboard design document — authoritative spec.
- **GDD §4.5**: Game-over conditions — 3 lives, no continue, score submission.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

- **Q1**: Main menu scope — Should this work item include creating the Main Menu scene (`src/scenes/MainMenuScene.ts`), or should that be a separate work item? The GDD references `src/ui/Menu.ts` ("Main menu, game-over screen") but it has not been implemented. The leaderboard must be "accessible from the main menu" per the work item description. **Assumption**: This work item creates the main menu scene with leaderboard access. If the producer disagrees, the main menu creation should be a separate work item, and the leaderboard should be accessible from the existing GymIndex instead (or from the game-over screen itself).

- **Q2**: Score tracking scope — Should this work item include implementing score tracking from scratch (enemy `scoreValue` assignment, score counter, HUD display, points on destroy), or should score tracking be a prerequisite completed by a separate work item? **Assumption**: Score tracking is included in scope — it is fundamental to the leaderboard feature.

- **Q3**: Initials input mechanism — How should the 3-character initials entry work? Options: (a) on-screen clickable keyboard (A-Z grid, neon-styled), (b) browser-native text input styled with CSS, (c) other mechanism. **Assumption**: On-screen clickable keyboard matching the neon terminal aesthetic.

- **Q4**: Enemy `scoreValue` values — What point values should each enemy type carry? Scout, Diver, Tank, Phaser, Swarm (per-unit), Boss? **Assumption**: Scout: 100, Diver: 150, Tank: 200, Phaser: 300, Swarm: 50, Boss: 1000. These can be tuned later via the game-rules config.

- **Q5**: Score format — Should the score display show formatted numbers (e.g., "50,000") or raw (e.g., "50000")? **Assumption**: Raw numeric display (no commas) matching the neon terminal aesthetic.

- **Q6**: Game-over flow — After submitting a score (or declining to submit), should the game-over screen offer a "Restart" button that returns to the main menu, or should it auto-restart? **Assumption**: "Restart" button returns to the main menu (or GymIndex if no main menu exists). "Play Again" is not available until a score is submitted or declined.

---

## Plan Clarifications (2026-09-22)

### Reconciled current state (verified against source)

The *Existing State* section above was written before the playable game landed.
The following are now **implemented** and are therefore *not* part of the remaining work:

- **Score tracking** — `PlayScene.SCORE_VALUES` awards points on enemy/boss destruction, `GameState.addScore()` accumulates them, and the score is rendered top-right in `PlayScene._buildHudText()` (`Score: N`). GDD §4.5 values are authoritative.
- **Game-over condition** — `PlayScene._loseLife()` calls `_finishRun(false)` when `lives <= 0`, transitioning to `GameOverScene` with the final score. There is no continue mechanic.
- **Main menu** — `MenuScene` exists (Play Game / Settings / Gym Scene Index) and is the boot scene (`gameConfig.ts`).
- **Initials entry** — `GameOverScene` implements the GDD §5.1 in-canvas keyboard model (A–Z, Backspace, exactly 3, Enter auto-submit) via the shared `FocusManager`.
- **Leaderboard stub** — `GameOverScene` contains `readLeaderboard()` / `saveScoreEntry()` persisting `{initials, score}` to `ai_hell_leaderboard`, displaying only the top 3. This is the placeholder this work item replaces.

### Producer decisions (2026-09-22)

- **Q1 — Scope:** confirmed. This work item covers the **remaining gap only** (leaderboard module, qualifying/skip UX, date, full display, menu access, stub retirement). It does not re-implement score tracking, game-over or the main menu.
- **Q2 — Initials input mechanism:** confirmed **keyboard entry only** (GDD §5.1). The earlier on-screen clickable-keyboard assumption is superseded — no on-screen keyboard is required.
- **Q3 — Main-menu access:** option **(a)**. Main-menu leaderboard access is in scope for this work item; AH-0MU9LJ52C00613RX is absorbed/relinked as a child so it is not duplicated.

### Interview record (2026-09-22, plan round 1)

- **Q1**: Scope this item to the *remaining gap*, not re-implementation? **Answer (producer):** yes — remaining gap. Final: yes.
- **Q2**: Confirm keyboard entry (GDD §5.1); no on-screen clickable keyboard? **Answer (producer):** confirmed. Final: keyboard-only.
- **Q3**: Main-menu leaderboard — (a) include here and absorb/relink AH-0MU9LJ52C00613RX, or (b) leave to that item? **Answer (producer):** (a). Final: include here.
- **OPEN QUESTION (resolved):** the automated effort/risk pre-check reported Extra Small / Low with a 0.0h degenerate placeholder; treated as unreliable and overridden in favour of full planning. Recorded in comment AH-C0MU6XUY0S001BIWP.

## Acceptance Criteria (revised, authoritative)

AC1–AC3 are retained as *already satisfied* and are verified by existing tests; they require no new work. AC4–AC6 are the remaining, testable acceptance criteria.

**Already satisfied (no remaining work):** AC1 score tracking (per-enemy `scoreValue`, HUD top-right; verified by `PlayScene`/`GameState`/HUD tests); AC2 game-over condition (lives reach 0 then final score, no continue; verified by `SceneNavigation.test.ts`); AC3 initials entry (3 uppercase A–Z, Enter auto-submit, keyboard-only per producer Q2; verified by `GameOverScene.test.ts`). These are recorded for completeness and are not covered by new child work items.

The remaining acceptance criteria are:

- **AC4 — Leaderboard persistence module** — `src/core/Leaderboard.ts` exports getEntries, addEntry, getTopN and isQualifying, storing `{rank, initials, score, date}` entries (max 10) under `ai_hell_leaderboard`.
- **AC5 — Qualifying and skip UX** — A qualifying score prompts for initials and persists on submit; a non-qualifying score shows an explanatory message and can be skipped with no write.
- **AC6 — Leaderboard display** — The game-over screen displays rank, initials, score and date for all up to 10 entries, highest first, and the main menu control displays the same full leaderboard.
